Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10

Summary: quick partner handoff to align GTM cadence, pre-demo checklist, and identify technical blockers for a pilot. Focus on routing, co-sell economics, and private deployment constraints.

Topics: 1) co-sell mechanics & lead routing 2) security/compliance questions (SOC2, SSO) 3) pilot scope and perf expectations 4) next steps and org owners

[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood here, joined by Priya our Solutions Eng and Evan, who will help on infra bits. How's everyone?
[00:12] Marta Reyes: Hi, Marta on my side. We're excited to move this along, thanks for setting up.
[00:17] Kenji Tanaka: Kenji, afternoon. Quick agenda ok?
[00:20] Jordan Miles: Yep, short agenda — handoff from partner team, quick GTM rhythm, then any technical flag we need before the demo.
[00:28] Samir Patel: Sounds good. We'll want to confirm data residency and the VPC pattern; our security folks flagged the KV cache and log retention approach last week.
[00:37] Priya Kapoor: Right, and we'll show the options — Hosted, Dedicated, Private — and the tradeoffs. For SlateBridge we think Dedicated or Private makes sense given the regulatory profile you described, but we'll validate.
[00:48] Leah Brooks: On procurement: we need a clear SOW and a ballpark for monthly committed spend to route approvals.
[00:55] Jordan Miles: Totally. Quick high-level: Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput with commit discounts; Private gives full VPC control and audit logs but has a longer procurement and deployment lead. We'll put dollar ranges in the GTM one-pager.
[01:12] Kenji Tanaka: What's the typical lead time for Private?
[01:16] Priya Kapoor: Usually 6-8 weeks from PO to boot for on-prem style installs; VPC private in cloud regions can be 3-4 weeks if networking is ready. Those are rough.
[01:27] Marta Reyes: Ok that timeline helps. For our co-sell we expect to do a joint webinar and a pilot with one customer first. We need to agree on touches and who owns the funnel.
[01:36] Jordan Miles: For routing, partner-sourced leads can go to your AE or we can take them into our funnel with attribution tags; co-sell credit terms are usually 10-20% of first-year ACV for partner-closed, but we're flexible depending on logos and volume.
[01:49] Kenji Tanaka: 10-20% makes sense as a starting point. We care about lead transparency — weekly reporting on pipeline and touches.
[01:58] Jordan Miles: We'll set up a shared pipeline view; propose weekly 30-min sync.
[02:02] Samir Patel: Technical: We heard 'KV cache' — what's the persistence? Do you keep any customer prompts beyond inference time?
[02:10] Priya Kapoor: Short answer: no long-term prompt persistence by default — we maintain transient KV cache for latency but can disable or encrypt at rest. We'll share the architecture doc. Note: our auto-prefix cache can reduce token costs but for PII flows we'd recommend cache bypass or keep it in customer-controlled HSM.
[02:32] Jordan Miles: I'll attach the private deployment checklist.
[02:35] Marta Reyes: Good — please include SSO/SAML flow and how audit logs are surfaced.
[02:40] Priya Kapoor: Will do. We have an audit log export that can be pushed to your SIEM; SAML SSO supported with SCIM provisioning in the console.
[02:49] Leah Brooks: Procurement question: do you accept Net 45 or Net 30? Also, do you require a master services agreement or can we do a POC addendum?
[02:57] Jordan Miles: We typically accept Net 30 on pilot contracts; enterprise committed contracts use Net 45 sometimes. We'll work with your team on the legal template — can try POC addendum first.
[03:07] Kenji Tanaka: On the pilot scope — what's realistic for a 4-week pilot from Redwood side?
[03:12] Priya Kapoor: For a 4-week pilot, we can provide a Hosted sandbox or Dedicated reserved instance. Expect to validate latency SLOs, throughput targets and basic quality evals. For Private, 4-week might be tight due to infra.
[03:26] Samir Patel: Our customer will run 150 req/s with median 100 tokens per response; cost projections become important. Do you have unit economics we can model?
[03:35] Jordan Miles: Yes — we'll share a cost sheet. In Dedicated you get lower per-token but fixed commit. Optimize features reduce cost further by batching and prefix cache (if acceptable). We'll put sample numbers in the perf spreadsheet.
[03:51] Marta Reyes: Competitors question — we've seen Anthropic and OpenAI proposals; how do you position versus them on reliability and TCO?
[03:59] Evan Chu: Redwood leans production-first — kernel selection, batching, smart routing so throughput per GPU tends to be better; net TCO often lower when you factor in stable latency and autoscaling. Also our rollout/fallback is opinionated which helps reliability during cloud blips.
[04:18] Jordan Miles: Quick note — Anthropic has higher model cost but simple dev ergonomics; OpenAI is broad but less control over deployment modes. We'll include a battlecard.
[04:28] Kenji Tanaka: Good. Any security hurdles we should expect?
[04:31] Priya Kapoor: SOC2 and ISO are common asks — we have SOC2 Type II and can share certificate; for extra compliance we offer private deployment and bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM.
[04:43] Samir Patel: For encryption, do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:46] Priya Kapoor: Yes, customer-managed keys in most cloud installs, and HSM in private/on-prem.
[04:52] Jordan Miles: Ok moving to demo prep — we need attendees and test data. Samir, what can your customer provide for a realistic test?
[04:59] Samir Patel: We can provide sanitized transcripts and a canonical prompt set. Note: some answers will require reranking, not pure generation.
[05:07] Priya Kapoor: We can demo reranking and tool-calls; will note that structured outputs sometimes need prompt engineering.
[05:13] Jordan Miles: We'll run the demo next week. Proposed times?
[05:16] Marta Reyes: Feb 18 or 19 preferably morning PST.
[05:20] Jordan Miles: We can do Feb 18 09:00 PST. I'll send invite after sync.
[05:24] Kenji Tanaka: Good. On joint assets — marketing webinar, playbook, and a one-pager: who owns content?
[05:30] Jordan Miles: Redwood can draft the one-pager and the first webinar slide deck; SlateBridge will own customer outreach and speaker slots. We'll do a joint preview.
[05:38] Marta Reyes: We'll want the slide deck 3 business days ahead to prep.
[05:42] Jordan Miles: Noted.
[05:44] Leah Brooks: Legal — any terms around data residency we must include? Our legal team will request a data processing addendum and subprocessor list.
[05:51] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide DPA and subprocessor list; DPA is standard and we can add region clauses for EU/US if needed.
[05:58] Samir Patel: Performance flags: if we go Dedicated, can you pin model versions and KV cache settings per route?
[06:05] Evan Chu: Yes, per-route fixtures and rollout policies — can canary to smaller percentage. Some of those names get munged in transcribes sometimes, but the feature exists.
[06:14] Jordan Miles: Quick aside — we should confirm the acceptance criteria for pilot. Marta, can you call out success metrics?
[06:20] Marta Reyes: Sure — 1) median latency under 350 ms for 95% of requests, 2) end-user quality score above baseline on 100 prompt set, 3) security review closed within two weeks of pilot start.
[06:31] Priya Kapoor: Good, we'll build the eval dashboard to show those.
[06:36] Jordan Miles: All right wrapping up, let me recap action items.
[06:40] Jordan Miles: Priya will share private deployment checklist and perf spreadsheet; Jordan will send GTM one-pager and draft co-sell economics; Marta to share compliance contacts; Leah to confirm procurement timing; schedule demo Feb 18 09:00 PST and technical deep dive Feb 17.
[06:58] Samir Patel: Confirming I'll provide sanitized prompts by 2026-02-14.
[07:04] Marta Reyes: We'll review and get back on any redlines on the terms.
[07:08] Jordan Miles: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and next steps.
